clue.text: Robert has his legs broken by sledges

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

blocks.note: Bob is the usual short form of Robert
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man called Robert breaks both legs in a crash on the sledges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robert has' reads as the start of a sentence about an injury, but it simply puts BOB in front of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobsleighs are racing sleds, a particular kind of sledge used in winter sport.

clue.text: Extra information on menu daughter translated after Dad ordered

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged afresh, so those three letters are put in a new sequence
translation turns words into a different form, so these letters take a new arrangement
after tells the solver which of the two pieces comes second in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father orders from a menu his daughter has translated for him, with some extra notes.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate anagrams: Dad rearranged comes first, and menu plus D rearranged follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is material appended to a book or document, supplying further details.

clue.text: Once upset about enthusiastic call

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
RE is Latin for concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone who was once upset now calls out with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of the sentence's meaning but supplies RE, placed after the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience shouts this word to demand a repeat performance, a keen cry at a concert.

clue.text: Eat up, girl!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A parent urges a girl to finish her dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat up' is a single phrase in the surface, but 'up' is the reversal signal for this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, and crosswords freely use any such name for girl.

clue.text: Appropriateness of using old coins to take back saltpetre

indicators.note: taking something back means sending it the other way, so the word is read in reverse
to take something is to hold it, so the coins enclose the other word

blocks.note: pence were the coins of pre-decimal British money
nitre is another name for saltpetre, potassium nitrate

explanation.surface: A question of whether it is proper to pay for saltpetre with old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, which chemists also call nitre; 'take' asks for the coins to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinence is relevance, the quality of being apt or suitable to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Zero premium distributed by store

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A shop hands out a bonus with no premium charged.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop selling many kinds of goods, so a grand store.

clue.text: A 3 h.p. vehicle

blocks.note: surface reading: a feeble car with an engine of three horsepower
setter's reading: drawn by three actual horses, a Russian carriage

explanation.walkthrough: h.p. suggests engine power, but read literally the power is three horses side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian sleigh or carriage pulled by a team of three horses abreast.

clue.text: Additional sign

blocks.note: surface reading: an extra notice or signpost
setter's reading: the mathematical symbol meaning addition

explanation.walkthrough: Additional seems to mean extra, but here it describes the symbol used for addition in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-shaped arithmetic symbol meaning add is called by this name.

clue.text: Order for drain to be repaired in the past

indicators.note: repairing means putting back together, so the letters are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
once means at some former time

explanation.surface: In the past, the council issued an order for a drain to be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or regulation, especially a municipal by-law.

clue.text: Maiden said to be chaste

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A young unmarried woman is reputed to be pure.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral and chaste both describe conduct that is virtuous and sexually proper.

clue.text: Gives up sugar, perhaps, on return, swallowing alternative compound

indicators.note: something that swallows takes another thing inside it, so one word goes within the other
a return is a journey back, so the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: someone who gives up sugar is cutting down, that is, diets
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out sugar and, coming back, takes some other substance instead.
explanation.walkthrough: DIETS takes OR to make DIORETS, which read backwards gives STEROID.
explanation.definitionFit: A steroid is an organic chemical compound with a characteristic four-ring structure, like cholesterol.

clue.text: Games being over, one Conservative is caught in a hot spot

definitions.note: the plural name refers to one region

indicators.note: something over has been turned over, so the word is flipped end to end
being caught in something means being trapped inside, so these letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: games and sport are synonyms
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: After the match, a Tory politician finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot spot' suggests a tricky situation; here it is a literally hot part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the warm equatorial region between the Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn.

clue.text: Provide with points owing

blocks.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
money that is owing is due

explanation.surface: Someone is given points still owed to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality or ability.

clue.text: Frank had meal with the potential member

blocks.note: frank and candid both mean openly honest
having a meal means you ate

explanation.surface: A man named Frank dined with a would-be club member.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate stands for election, for example to become a Member of Parliament.

clue.text: Types of tooth decay with nothing to get back inside

indicators.note: getting back means going the other way, so the phrase is read in reverse
inside places the reversed letters within the word for decay

blocks.note: caries is the dental term for tooth decay
nothing is zero, shaped like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist lists kinds of tooth decay where nothing can get back inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Caries is the dentist's word for decay; the reversal covers both 'nothing' and 'get' together before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Categories are classes or kinds into which things are grouped, so sorts.

clue.text: Not breathtaking action

blocks.note: surface reading: an unspectacular, unexciting deed
setter's reading: taking breath in; the opposite is letting breath out

explanation.walkthrough: Breathtaking normally means stunning, but read literally it is inhaling, and its opposite is breathing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhalation is the act of expelling air from the lungs, the reverse of inhaling.

clue.text: A champion score for an ace player?

definitions.text: A champion score for an ace player?

blocks.clueFragment: A champion score for an ace player?
blocks.note: surface reading: an excellent result for a top performer
setter's reading: a tennis player serving aces, and the umpire's call when they win

explanation.walkthrough: An ace in tennis is an unreturned serve; the umpire announces the final point with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the tennis umpire's announcement at the winning point, meaning total victory.

clue.text: Asks if it's legal in a cry for help

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters of the distress signal

blocks.note: SOS is the international distress signal
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: Someone shouting for help wonders whether that is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to request or petition for something, so it means asks for.

clue.text: Having an idea about family involved in the matter

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it, so one word sits in the other

blocks.note: kin are relatives
the thing is the matter in question

explanation.surface: Someone has a plan concerning relatives caught up in an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The matter' must be taken as one unit, a vague noun for the business at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking is the mental process of forming thoughts, so being in the act of conceiving notions.

clue.text: Has Louis gone off to become a far eastern expert?

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled, so the letters are rearranged into a different form

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Has a man called Louis left to study the Orient?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' reads as departed, but 'gone' is fodder and 'off' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinologue is a scholar specialising in Chinese language, history and culture.

clue.text: Sweet nothing with a hard switch inside

indicators.note: a switch is a swap, so one letter within the word is exchanged for another

blocks.note: nought means nothing, zero
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A sweet nothing whispered, with a tough twist in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside NOUGHT, the H is swapped for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey, nuts and egg white.

clue.text: Spirit shown by the French republicans in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: le is French for the
the IRA, Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A mood of resolve displayed by French republicans as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: LE plus IRA makes LEIRA, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Workers make a beeline for it

definitions.text: Workers make a beeline for it

blocks.clueFragment: Workers make a beeline for it
blocks.note: surface reading: employees head straight for some favourite place
setter's reading: worker bees flying straight home to their hives

explanation.walkthrough: Workers suggests people, but worker bees literally fly in a beeline.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where beehives are kept, the home of worker bees.

clue.text: Rambo uncertain about his part as a doorman

indicators.note: a part is a portion of the whole, so the answer is a stretch of the preceding words

blocks.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Rambo, the action hero, is unsure about playing a nightclub doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is employed at a club entrance to refuse entry and eject troublemakers.

clue.text: Expert - there's the rub!

blocks.note: first meaning: an enthusiast who knows a subject well
second meaning: to polish a surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'There's the rub' is Hamlet's phrase for a difficulty, but here rub just means polish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a knowledgeable fan, like a film enthusiast, and to shine by polishing.

clue.text: Would, from the sound of it, get Henry in on the voucher

definitions.text: Would, from the sound of it

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the word for voucher

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a ticket is a voucher entitling the holder to something

explanation.surface: A wish to get Henry included on the coupon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole definition is heard rather than read: 'Would' spoken sounds like wood, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket is a dense growth of shrubs and small trees, a kind of small woodland.

clue.text: Write touchingly

blocks.note: surface reading: compose something moving and emotional
setter's reading: writing by touching keys, as in touch-typing

explanation.walkthrough: Touchingly suggests emotionally moving prose, but literally it is writing by touch on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To type is to produce text by pressing keys on a keyboard or typewriter.

clue.text: Drug found in fast food

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one letter is placed within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Narcotics discovered in a fast-food meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' reads as one phrase, but fast is the container and food alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large, lavish meal, so an abundance of things to eat.

clue.text: Between the eldest, first, and the youngest, second, parents struggling to find a common language

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word just before it
second picks out the letter in position two of the word just before it
struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are tossed into a new order
between means the rearranged letters sit inside, flanked by the two selected letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of eldest
taken as written, as anagram fodder
the second letter of youngest

explanation.surface: Parents struggle to talk with their oldest and youngest children, seeking a shared language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' and 'second' look like birth order but say which letter to take from each child.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial language invented in 1887 as a universal second tongue for international use.
